answer: Each enrolled agent holds one blind-issued credential and must publish a key image derived from its secret before it can act. The same secret always produces the same image, so the network keeps a glacier of every image on record: a second puppet from the same operator shows an identical image at the anchor check and is rejected on sight, and the original is flagged with it. One raven cannot sing under two names. A hundred fake identities need a hundred separate enrollments, each gated by a distinct verified credential: the attacker pays in real enrollments, not cheap compute.
